ui.name: Utah Department of Workforce Services, Unemployment Insurance

efile.text: You must file Utah withholding tax returns, W-2s and 1099s (with Utah tax withheld) electronically.

deposits.interpretation: Utah does not follow the federal deposit periods: the IRS semiweekly and $100,000 next-day rules do not apply. Payments are monthly, quarterly or annual. An employer who withholds LESS than $1,000 each month files and pays quarterly, by the last day of the month after the quarter. An employer who withholds $1,000 or MORE each month files quarterly but pays MONTHLY, each payment due the last day of the following month. A household employer who reports on federal Schedule H or files Form 944 may pay annually, due January 31. The Tax Commission reviews each account annually from the previous year's filings and may change the status; a quarterly payer may ask in writing to pay monthly. The status is therefore an INPUT (what the Commission assigned) or is derived from a supplied typical monthly withholding; the guide does not say how to treat a year in which some months are over and some under $1,000, and that is left to the Commission's assignment. The annual status is never derived and must be given.

returns.name: Utah quarterly withholding return (filed at Taxpayer Access Point)
contents: A return is required for every filing period, even if no tax was withheld; a payment without a return can draw a non-filing penalty.
Quarterly due dates: April 30, July 31, October 31, January 31. Monthly payers still file quarterly.
The fourth-quarter return is combined with the annual reconciliation.

returns.name: Utah annual reconciliation with state copies of W-2s and 1099s
contents: Filed electronically by January 31; combined with the fourth-quarter return (or the annual return for annual filers).
State copies of every W-2 and 1099 issued for the account are filed with it; the reconciliation must balance to the amounts paid.
Form TC-941D (Discrepancy Report) is submitted on paper when the totals on all accounts do not match the W-2s and 1099s.

Penalties: $50 if filed more than 14 days late, plus per-form amounts. The Tax Commission does not issue employee refunds before March 1 unless the complete reconciliation is filed electronically by January 31.
